top_categories.workout_context: The Divide's mixed terrain forces constant power changes. Surge over the rough stuff, settle on the smooth, repeat for 52 miles.
87ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.
Race-pace efforts that mimic The Divide's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before race day.
At The Divide, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of The Divide. Train it until it feels boring.
Varied gradients on mixed terrain demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At The Divide, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.
52 miles on mixed terrain burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
Double-threshold training builds sustained power with less fatigue. More FTP per hour of training.
Smooth pedaling at 52 miles saves muscle. Bad technique at mile 10 is invisible. At mile 80 it's a cramp.
When someone attacks on mixed terrain, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
Low-cadence force work for 4,500ft of climbing. The slow, grinding ascents where you can't spin—you push.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 40–60g carbs/hour for The Divide’s 50 miles. Front-load calories in the first half. One bottle per hour minimum, more in heat.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at The Divide requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Gravel Specific, TT Threshold, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 52 miles of mixed terrain in Manton, Michigan, United States.
